scope: Read-only source and existing test review; no new execution or production edits
verdict: No concrete correctness defect found in the reviewed ownership, identity, generation, ranges, typed DT commit or scoped-loan boundaries.

reviewed_invariants.ownership: Private Box/exclusive mutable-slice backing is consumed; aperture length derives from observed slice; no safe resize/rebase/raw-pointer constructor.
reviewed_invariants.token_liveness: Nonzero monotonic process-local owner IDs and reservation serials; foreign/released/reused tokens checked before byte access. Generation exhaustion occurs before effects.
reviewed_invariants.allocation: Power-of-two guest alignment, checked bounds and live capacity intersection. First-fit moves beyond overlapping extents without skipping any feasible earlier placement; existing byte-scan2000-step oracle independently checks policy.
reviewed_invariants.copy_atomicity: Range/usize conversion and next generation preflight precede the single copy. Readonly input cannot safely alias the exclusive backing; returned errors leave bytes and generation unchanged.
reviewed_invariants.dt_commit: Existing immutable MaterializedTree source binding is preserved unchanged. Bind/commit both validate current stamp, owner, live destination, purpose, alignment and complete fit; commit consumes prepared output without caller-redirection coordinates.
reviewed_invariants.execution_loan: HRTB FnOnce return type is independent of temporary loan lifetime; generation advances before callback. Existing compile-fail cases cover owner lifetime, escaping RAM and escaping borrowed service. Writes on callback error intentionally persist and are separately documented/tested.
reviewed_invariants.snapshot: Borrowed live records prohibit concurrent mutation; detached stamps become stale after every ledger mutation/execution loan.

limits: No actual EFI consumer execution in this review or this ledger slice.
Guest-address alignment does not claim host allocation page alignment.
Purpose tags and current snapshot stamps do not prove semantic provenance of arbitrary provider-value bytes; target schemas and ABI remain caller-owned.
Scoped execution can modify all RAM and does not roll back on an error; reservations are staging records, not runtime access permissions.
Process-local identity requires the documented 64-bit atomic targets and is not a serialized/cross-process capability.
